A1.justification: Both complete 15-page PDFs describe the same Flow2GAN work. The text, equations, figures, tables and Appendix A.1–A.4 are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original audio-generation benchmarks, ablations, inference timings and zero-shot TTS results, including supplementary results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendix.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 retain the same endpoint-prediction objective, spectral energy-adaptive loss, GAN fine-tuning procedure and three-branch ConvNeXt architecture. The 1/2/4-step variants already existed in v1.

E1.justification: Both retain LibriTTS Mel-conditioned vocoding, EnCodec-conditioned universal audio using the same speech/music/sound datasets, and F5-TTS evaluation on LibriSpeech-PC. No dataset, task or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every corresponding experiment, including BigVGAN/v2, Vocos, RFWave, PeriodWave-Turbo, WaveFM, EnCodec, MBD, pure GAN training and Shortcut models.

E3.justification: The splits, preprocessing, metrics, training budgets, model configurations, codec bandwidths and timing/TTS procedures in Section 5 and Appendix A are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the loss and architecture ablations, training comparisons, noisy-conditioning TTS test, multi-step sampling analysis and Mel versus log-Mel comparison (Tables 3–6, 8–9 and 11). No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: MOS/SMOS uncertainty reporting in Tables 1–2 is identical. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-definition or statistical-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–9 and 11 and the qualitative examples in Figure 2 are unchanged. For example, Table 1's four-step Flow2GAN PESQ remains 4.484.

T1.justification: The Flow Matching definitions, endpoint-objective derivation, sampling rule and energy-scaled loss in Equations 1–6 are identical. No assumptions, proofs or mathematical arguments are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion soften explicit claims of 'better' quality-efficiency trade-offs to 'highly favorable' comparisons. The abstract and conclusion explicitly foreground the existing 1/2/4-step variants; the central contributions and capability scope remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The detailed interpretations, mechanism explanations and qualifications in Sections 4–5 are unchanged. The mode-collapse caution omitted from the abstract remains in the introduction, so it is not removed from the paper.

D1.justification: v1's abstract already advertises released code, but its reproducibility statement promises code and checkpoints upon acceptance. v2 states that both are publicly available at the existing repository. This updates the documented release status; implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography are unchanged, including the positioning relative to Vocos, PriorGrad, RFWave and PeriodWave-Turbo. No cited work or novelty argument is added or removed.

P1.justification: Localized edits affect the abstract, introduction, conclusion and reproducibility statement. The header changes from 'Under review' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026'; section organization and appendices remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All three figures and eleven tables retain their content and design. Visual changes are limited to publication headers, the arXiv version/date stamp and small spacing or reflow adjustments on edited pages.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves v1's inconsistent release wording and explicitly documents checkpoint availability, modestly improving reproducibility guidance. The less categorical summary claims also better accommodate the mixed comparisons in Tables 1–2 and 7. Methods and empirical evidence are unchanged; repository availability is reported by the PDF, not independently verified.
